name: The Ritz-Carlton, Amelia Island
positioning: Oceanfront resort on a barrier island, with ocean-view balconies, an on-site golf club and tennis programs
best_for: Travelers who want an ocean-view room with golf and tennis on site
Families and nature lovers who like naturalist-led experiences

facts.text: The resort sits on a secluded barrier island.
Every guestroom and suite has a private balcony and ocean views.
The Ritz-Carlton Suite is a one-bedroom suite with a fireplace in the living area and a formal dining area seating six.
Three private boardwalks lead guests to the oceanfront, buffered by sand dunes and sea oats.
The Golf Club of Amelia Island has an 18-hole course designed by Mark McCumber and Gene Littler.
Coquina serves Latin cuisine focused on seafood and coastal dishes inspired by the island's Eight Flags heritage.
Tidewater Grill is a casual restaurant serving lunch, dinner and drinks.
The resort partners with tennis coach Patrick Mouratoglou for training camps, private lessons and retreats.

highlights.text: Guests can join the resort marine biologist to locate, track and record dolphin behavior for a research study on the Amelia River and Cumberland Sound.
In the Hook, Line & Supper experience, guests fish with the Executive Chef on the Amelia River.
Beach horseback riding along the Atlantic shore is available, and Amelia Island is one of the few places where it is permitted.
The Nature Center has three on-site Naturalists specializing in marine science and biology.

considerations.text: Enhancement work is scheduled from October 2026 into early 2027, including select public restrooms, the function space and the main pool; guests keep access to one of the resort's two pools throughout.
The hotel does not have an airport shuttle to Fernandina Beach Municipal Airport.
The resort is exclusively cashless; guests present a credit card at check-in.
